title: The Burn Rate and Cash Runway

parts.visual:
A startup raises $2 Million. The CEO hires 10 engineers, rents a fancy office, and throws a huge launch party. Six months later, the bank account hits $0. The CEO is shocked. The company dies instantly.

The Survival Metrics:
1. The Burn Rate: The exact amount of cash the startup loses every single month (Total Expenses minus Total Revenue).
2. The Runway: The amount of time (in months) the startup has before it goes completely bankrupt. (Total Cash divided by Burn Rate).
parts.audio: As a founder, your primary job is not writing code; your primary job is not running out of money. If you do not know your exact burn rate and runway down to the specific day, you are flying a plane blindfolded.

questions.question: A startup has $1,000,000 in the bank. They spend $150,000 a month on salaries, and make $50,000 a month in revenue. What is their 'Net Burn Rate'?
options: $100,000 a month. The 'Net Burn' is the actual cash lost after revenue is factored in ($150k expenses - $50k revenue = $100k net loss).
questions.correct_answer: $100,000 a month. The 'Net Burn' is the actual cash lost after revenue is factored in ($150k expenses - $50k revenue = $100k net loss).
questions.explanation: Gross burn is what you spend. Net burn is what you lose.

questions.question: Listen to the CFO's warning to the CEO. What is the critical error the CEO is making regarding the Runway?
questions.tts_text: We have 12 months of runway left. But you want to start fundraising in month 11. That is suicide. Fundraising takes 6 months. If we start in month 11, we will miss payroll and die before the VC check clears.
options: The CEO wants to buy a boat.

Waiting too long to fundraise. A founder must always initiate the next round of fundraising when they have at least 6 to 9 months of runway left. Raising money when you are desperate destroys your negotiation power.
The CFO is bad at math.
questions.correct_answer: Waiting too long to fundraise. A founder must always initiate the next round of fundraising when they have at least 6 to 9 months of runway left. Raising money when you are desperate destroys your negotiation power.
questions.explanation: Never raise money when you are bleeding.

questions.question: What is the fastest, most brutal way to decrease the Burn Rate to survive a crisis?
options: A Reduction in Force (Layoffs). In a software startup, 80% of the expenses are usually employee salaries. You cannot cut your way to survival by stopping free coffee; you must cut headcount.
questions.correct_answer: A Reduction in Force (Layoffs). In a software startup, 80% of the expenses are usually employee salaries. You cannot cut your way to survival by stopping free coffee; you must cut headcount.

questions.question: Why do VCs actually *encourage* a high burn rate in the early stages?
options: Because they are buying speed. VCs do not invest in a startup so it can survive as a 'zombie' company for 10 years. They want the startup to burn the cash aggressively to hire top engineers and capture the market before competitors do.
Because high burn rates look cool.
questions.correct_answer: Because they are buying speed. VCs do not invest in a startup so it can survive as a 'zombie' company for 10 years. They want the startup to burn the cash aggressively to hire top engineers and capture the market before competitors do.
questions.explanation: Venture capital is rocket fuel. You either achieve orbit or explode.
